reasoning.text: Base rate/reference class: for this same seasonally adjusted Canada LFS unemployment-rate variant, the recent first-print reference class is Dec 2025-May 2026 values of 6.8, 6.5, 6.7, 6.7, 6.9, and 6.6. The level base rate is persistence near the latest 6.6 rather than the older 2017-2019 average of 6.0, because StatCan says unemployment has remained above that pre-pandemic average since spring 2024.

Prior/update/interval: persistence prior = May 2026 first-print unemployment rate 6.6. Historical sample = successive monthly changes from Dec 2025 to May 2026: -0.3, +0.2, 0.0, +0.2, -0.3 percentage points. sigma = 0.25 using sample standard deviation of those changes. Approximate 80% normal half-width = 1.28*sigma = 1.28*0.25 = 0.32 percentage points; the sample is short, but the resulting width matches recent LFS month-to-month dispersion. Adjustment components: level +0.00 from persistence, momentum +0.05 because the May drop partly reversed April's jump, one-off -0.05 because May employment rose 88,000 and job-finding improved, policy/mechanism +0.05 for still-soft hiring and tariff uncertainty. Combined mean = 6.6 + 0.05 = 6.65, rounded first-print point = 6.7; 6.65 +/- 0.32 gives 6.33 to 6.97, rounded interval = 6.3 to 7.0.

Counter-consideration: upside risk is a renewed participation rise or tariff-linked hiring freeze that pushes unemployment back to April's 6.9 or above; downside risk is another broad May-like employment gain, especially in Ontario, British Columbia, construction, or services, that pulls the rate toward 6.3. A June print at or below 6.2 or at or above 7.1 would land outside the interval.
